title: Filesystems in Go
summary: Build a tiny filesystem on an in-memory block device: superblock, block bitmap, inodes, directories, an fsck, and a journal that survives a crash at every write.
description: Build and audit a small filesystem model in standard-library Go. The first three lessons implement a 64-byte block-device format, allocation bitmap and direct-block inodes. Later checkpoints isolate directory encoding, ownership consistency checks, exhaustive crash-prefix replay, safe replacement ordering and redo-journal recovery. The directory and recovery exercises use explicit simplified interfaces rather than a complete mounted filesystem. Crash replay assumes atomic, ordered writes; the journal capstone assumes a complete durable record list and an atomic commit marker, then tests failure at every home-write boundary. Torn writes, concurrent transactions, device caches and journal serialization are outside the model. Everything is deterministic and in memory.
outcomes: Encode and validate a superblock, bitmap, inodes and directory records.
Classify orphan, duplicate, dangling and invalid block references without trusting metadata.
Enumerate every write-prefix crash point and preserve initialized allocated data through replacement.
Replay a committed metadata journal idempotently after interrupted home writes.
